name: Komi-Zyrian
confidence_why: Itkonen 1955 and Lytkin 1970 agree that in Komi-Yazva stress falls on the first syllable with a non-high vowel and on the last syllable when every vowel is high, but that is the Yazva lect (listed by Glottolog as a separate language), and Lytkin 1970 describes Komi-Zyrian proper as having free stress with only a tendency toward the first syllable, so the rule is secure for Yazva and does not describe Komi-Zyrian as a whole. 3 further first-hand descriptions conflict (see the conflicting-description items); the entry follows Itkonen 1955 1955.

audit.recode_to: Split: move the present Itkonen 1955:28-29 / Lytkin 1961 vowel-quality ('leftmost heavy = non-high vowel, else final') record to komi1277 Komi-Yazva; code komi1268 Komi-Zyrian as quantity-insensitive initial stress, weak/non-obligatory (Lytkin 1970:248 'тенденция ставить ударение на первый слог, однако это необязательно'; Estill 2006:75-76 94.6-97.6% initial in read speech; Itkonen 1955:29-30; LES 1990), with a note on dialectal stem/suffix-conditioned deviations (Izhma minimal pairs pemda· ~ pe·mda, Itkonen 1955:30; Luza-Letka -ал attraction, Lytkin 1970:251). Not weight-sensitive, not unbounded.
audit.reasoning: (1) Quote verified verbatim in the Itkonen 1955 file we hold at pp. 28-29 (text ll. 389-431 and the p. 29 page scan). (2) But the passage describes 'Ostpermjakisch' = Komi-Yazva, which Glottolog 5.x lists as a separate language komi1277 (checked on glottolog.org); the StressTyp2 entry for this language 'Yazva' and WALS 'yzv' were inherited under language 766 Komi-Zyrian and the roster key komi1268, and the the compilers flagged this in the current catalog, yet the public record is named 'Komi-Zyrian' with a weight-sensitive unbounded rule. Every source opened for Komi-Zyrian proper says otherwise: Itkonen 1955:29-30 (same copies we hold) treats 'die eigentliche Komi-Sprache' separately (varied; stem stress in some dialects); Lytkin 1970:248 (downloaded now, open, page scan read) says Komi-Zyrian has only a tendency to initial stress and the speaker may stress any syllable; Estill 2006 (held, unused) measures 9

sources.citation: Rédei, Károly (1988). Die Syrjänische Sprache. In The Uralic languages: description, history and foreign influences. Leiden: E.~J.~Brill. pp. 111-130.

sources.quote: Betonung. Das Syrjänische kennt die sogenannte freie Betonung, d.h. die Betonung kann auf jede beliebige Silbe fallen, ohne die Bedeutung des Wortes zu verändern. Z.B.: [múnęni̮ ~ munę́ni̮ ~ munęní̮ — three accentuations of the same word, accent marks garbled in scanned] ,sie gehen'. Im allgemeinen ist die Betonung jedoch auf der ersten Silbe. Diese Tendenz ist auch bei den alten russischen Lehnwörtern in der syrjänischen Sprache zu beobachten. Z.B.: sáldat ,Soldat' (< ru. солдат), t'él'ega ,Wagen' (< ru. телега). || Vowel length (p. 114): Es gibt nur kurze Vokale. Die emphatische bzw. die durch die Betonung eintretende Dehnung hat keinen phonematischen Wert.
sources.locator: printed p. 116, section 'Betonung'; vowel-length sentence printed p. 114
sources.note: Rédei's deciding statement for the Komi-Zyrian literary variety (Middle Vychegda, Syktyvkar): so-called free stress, stress may fall on any syllable without changing meaning (the same word 'sie gehen' shown with stress on each of its three syllables), but in general on the first syllable; the initial tendency is also seen in old Russian loans (sáldat, t'él'ega). No weight, vowel-height or quantity condition is stated; vowels are all short and stress-induced lengthening is non-phonemic (p. 114). Secondary stress: not mentioned. sources.quote: Die Betonung ist ganz der finnischen gleich, d. h. der Hauptaccent faellt regelmaessig auf die erste Sylbe, und in laengeren Woertern haben die dritte und fuenfte einen schwaecheren Nebenaccent, was der Sprache den in allen finnischen und esthnischen Poesien durchklingenden trochaeischen Rythmus giebt.
sources.locator: Lautlehre par. 1, printed p. 15; restated in par. 5, printed p. 18: 'Der eigentliche Wortstamm bildet den Anfang jedes Wortes, und auf die erste Sylbe desselbe…
sources.note: Wiedemann states fixed initial main stress with weaker secondary stress on the 3rd and 5th syllables (trochaic), no weight, no exceptions, nothing on tone. The catalog codes komi1268 as weight-hedged (vowel-aperture weight, secondary stress 'not mentioned in the source') from Komi-Yazva sources (Itkonen 1955 'Yazva', Lytkin 1961 Komi-Yazva dialect); Wiedemann describes Zyrian proper (Ust-Sysolsk dialect), so the disagreement is variety-level (Yazva vs Sysola Zyrian) rather than two descriptions of the same variety. sources.citation: Castrén, Matthias Alexander (1844). Elementa grammatices syrjaenae. Helsingforsiae: Es officina typ. heredum Simelii. 166 pp.
sources.access_detail: open copy posted by the author (located 2026-09-25); a digital copy (available on request)
sources.quote: Accentus linguae Syrjaenae, ut aliarum linguarum ejusdem originis, cadit in syllabas impares: primam, tertiam, quintam e. s. p.; in primam fortius, in alias vero adeo molliter, ut auri vix capiatur. Nonnulla disyllabica nomina, desinentia in vocalem, amittunt vim accentus in prima syllaba ob nimis acutam in secunda adspirationem. Haec sola sua adspiratione distinguuntur a verbis in prima persona Praesentis Indicativi; ex. gr. pemda', tenebrae, pemda, tenebresco; jugda', claritas, jugda, claresco; sjökta', gravitas, sjökta, gravor (cfr. §. 2). [§23:] Quantitas linguae Syrjaenae non est tam lenis et incerta, quam linguae Lapponicae, sed clara et distincta, ut linguae Finnicae. Occurrit frequentissime in prima verbi syllaba; ubi aliquando in ceteris invenitur, semper contractione orta esse videtur.
sources.locator: Part II 'De accentu et quantitate', §22, printed p. 15; §23 printed pp. 15-16; cross-refs §2 printed p. 2 and §16 printed p. 13
sources.note: System stated: accent on the odd syllables (1st, 3rd, 5th..), strongest on the first, the others 'so soft that the ear scarcely catches them' (secondary stress stated, alternating, very weak). Exception class: some disyllabic vowel-final nouns lose the first-syllable accent because of a sharp final 'aspiration' (§2/§16: an h heard after the last vowel of such nouns, from an earlier s or k, e.g. vo' year ~ Finnish vuosi), so noun pemda' 'darkness' vs verb pemda 'I grow dark', jugda' 'brightness' vs jugda, sjökta' 'heaviness' vs sjökta; §2 adds that the aspiration is dropped in inflection. Acta Linguistica Academiae Scientiarum Hungaricae 20(3-4): 245-263. Open whole-volume scan, REAL-J MTAKhttps://real-j.mtak.hu/823/1/ACTALINGV_20.pdf
sources.quote: p. 248: 'В коми-зырянском языке имеется тенденция ставить ударение на первый слог, однако это необязательно: говорящий произвольно может ставить на любой слог даже при изолированном произношении слова: ко́кьямыс~кокья́мыс 'восемь', ве́тымын~веты́мын~ветымы́н 'пятьдесят', ко́травны~котра́вны~котравны́ 'бегать'.' (Komi-Zyrian grouped with Erzya as 'absolutely free' stress with an initial tendency). p. 250: 'Идеальным примером, где место ударения зависит от фонетического фактора, является коми-язьвинский диалект. В неодносложных словах этого диалекта ударение не падает на гласные исконно верхнего
sources.locator: p. 248 (Komi-Zyrian; p. 270 of the volume, page scan read); p. 250 (Komi-Yazva; p. 272); p. 251 (Luza/Letka dialect suffix -ал attraction); pp. 261-262 (Komi 'лишь тенденция ставить акцент на 1-й слог'; Komi-Zyrian 'отчасти' absolutely free)
sources.note: Lytkin's own typology: Komi-Zyrian = initial tendency, non-obligatory, speaker may stress any syllable (p. 248); Komi-Yazva = 'quality-vocalic' stress (p. 250). Directly separates the two lects the record conflates.
